title: Aaron Judge Sparks Offense as Yankees Clinch Playoff Spot
seoTitle: Yankees Clinch Playoff Spot as Aaron Judge Returns
subtitle: The captain's first home run after injury fuels the team's postseason qualification
excerpt: Aaron Judge, back from a rib fracture, hit his first home run since May 24, helping the Yankees secure their 61st playoff berth in history.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Aaron Judge's first run since May 24 arrived at a decisive moment: a three-run home run in the eighth inning secured an 8-3 victory over Minnesota and sealed the New York Yankees' 61st playoff qualification.

The home run that changed the game

With two outs, Spencer Jones was at bat when Judge, back after more than three months sidelined by a rib fracture, hit the ball against A.J. Minter. The batter, who had gone 3-for-20 with 11 strikeouts since his return, sent the ball out of the park, extending the lead to 7-2.

Yankees' historic qualification

With the victory, the team secured at least an American League Wild Card spot, marking their ninth qualification in ten seasons. The franchise reached 61 postseason berths, a record number in MLB history.

Judge's return from injury

The Yankees' captain, a three-time American League MVP, missed 84 games due to a stress fracture in his right rib. His return occurred last week, and the home run was his first since early May.

Impact on team statistics

With Judge on the field, the team averaged 5.17 runs per game and a .243 batting average, in addition to 86 home runs. Without him, the average dropped to 3.93 runs and a .228 batting average, with 107 home runs in total.

Manager's comments

Manager Aaron Boone highlighted the team's effort: "You work hard to have the opportunity to make the playoffs. I'm pleased because the team looks better than I expected. He is hitting the right pitches and avoiding unnecessary chases."

With information from WRAL.
